section_summary: This section concerns American copyrights and alleged book piracy in Japan, including unauthorized translations and imported reprints. Much of it follows McGraw-Hill’s correspondence with the State Department and the American Embassy about pirated technical books sold in Osaka. Other documents concern translations of Pearl Buck’s work, Margaret Mitchell Marsh’s copyright interests, and a dispute over the Japanese periodical Japan News-Week.

subfiles.title: Register of Copyrights’ comments on American copyrights in Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s translation rights under the 1905 treaty and the Berne Convention.
subfiles.summary: The Register questions whether denouncing the treaty would benefit American authors and says Japan’s position should not govern United States adherence to Berne.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill reply concerning American copyrights in Japan
subfiles.from: Curtis W. McGraw, McGraw-Hill Book Company
subfiles.about: Thanks McClure for an Embassy report and requests information on piracy of McGraw-Hill books.
subfiles.summary: McGraw-Hill appreciates the report but still seeks information on unauthorized editions of its books in Japan.

subfiles.title: Department letter forwarding McGraw-Hill’s response
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards McGraw-Hill’s response and its request for further information on unauthorized editions.
subfiles.summary: The Department sends the company’s reply to the Embassy for its information.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Pearl Buck translations
subfiles.about: Draws attention to a Japan Advertiser clipping concerning a translation of The Good Earth.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum connects the clipping to an earlier Embassy list of unauthorized Pearl Buck translations.

subfiles.title: Suit Initiated by Good Earth Translator Given to Procurators, With New Charge
subfiles.about: Reports a dispute over credit and royalties for a Japanese translation of The Good Earth.
subfiles.summary: Shosaku Fukazawa sued Kaku Nii and publisher manager Yukuo Haruyama after Nii was credited for Fukazawa’s translation. Police reportedly found no evidence of fraud but referred possible criminal misrepresentation under copyright law to procurators.

subfiles.title: Department letter concerning Margaret Mitchell Marsh
subfiles.about: Forwards part of a letter from the author of Gone With the Wind for Embassy comment.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests any pertinent Embassy observations but gives no instruction.

subfiles.title: Coulson inquiry about Japan News-Week
subfiles.about: Asks whether an effective remedy exists against a Japanese periodical using a name like Newsweek.
subfiles.summary: Coulson encloses an unanswered objection sent to the Japanese publisher and asks about unfair competition remedies.

subfiles.title: Objection to the title Japan News-Week
subfiles.about: Objects to Japan News-Week’s title on behalf of the publisher of Newsweek.
subfiles.summary: The lawyers assert trademark and copyright interests and request a title change to avoid confusion.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Coulson’s complaint
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the complaint about Japan News-Week.
subfiles.summary: McClure says the Department will consider whether a remedy is available.

subfiles.title: Renewed Newsweek complaint
subfiles.about: Renews concern that Japan News-Week could be confused with Newsweek in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Coulson cites press coverage that could confuse readers and harm his client’s reputation. He asks about remedies under treaties with Japan before seeking to block imports under Treasury regulations.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Newsweek Backs Roosevelt Blast at Nazis
subfiles.about: Reports political commentary attributed to the Japanese periodical Newsweek.
subfiles.summary: Two copies of the clipping report the Japanese periodical’s proposal to reconsider Japan’s Tripartite Pact position and seek a compromise with the United States.

subfiles.title: International News Service release on Japanese Newsweek
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese periodical’s views on the Tripartite Pact and relations with the United States.
subfiles.summary: The release is the source material for the accompanying newspaper clipping.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: Records circulation of file 894.544.
subfiles.summary: File charge entries and dates.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: Records circulation of file 894.544.
subfiles.summary: Additional file charge entries.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on Gone With the Wind
subfiles.about: Points to another file on foreign translation rights for Gone With the Wind.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an inquiry about protection in Japan.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill copyright infringement file jacket
subfiles.about: Labels the McGraw-Hill infringement case.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for McGraw-Hill copyrights in Japan.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill inquiry about pirated books
subfiles.about: Seeks advice about technical books reportedly pirated in China and sold in Japan.
subfiles.summary: McGraw encloses a confidential report from Maruzen and asks whether treaty protection or a formal complaint could address sales of the alleged reprints.

subfiles.title: Maruzen report on reprints sold in Osaka
subfiles.about: Reports cheap reprints of McGraw-Hill books sold by an Osaka bookseller.
subfiles.summary: Maruzen suspects printing in Tianjin, lists titles and prices, and asks that its role as informant remain confidential.

subfiles.title: McClure requests copyright and confidentiality details
subfiles.about: Asks whether the books have Japanese copyright protection and whether Maruzen permits Embassy inquiries.
subfiles.summary: McClure seeks facts before recommending action and notes that United States adherence to the revised Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works might strengthen protection.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill reply on English copyright
subfiles.about: Explains that McGraw-Hill copyrights its books in England and proposes seeking evidence from Maruzen.
subfiles.summary: McGraw hopes English copyright may support protection in Japan. He offers to ask Maruzen about confidentiality and to obtain a suspected reprint.

subfiles.title: McClure on simultaneous publication and Embassy inquiry
subfiles.about: Explains how publication in England might affect copyright protection in Japan.
subfiles.summary: McClure asks whether the books appeared in England within two weeks of United States publication. He is forwarding the correspondence to the Embassy with instructions to protect Maruzen and seeks evidence of where the reprints were printed.

subfiles.title: Department instruction on McGraw-Hill piracy
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Directs a cautious inquiry into alleged McGraw-Hill piracy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department forwards correspondence and tells the Embassy to avoid exposing Maruzen without consent. It asks whether reprints are made in Japan or imported from China and whether simultaneous publication in a convention country gives American books protection in Japan.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on McGraw-Hill infringement
subfiles.about: Reports Maruzen’s account of pirated technical books sold by an Osaka bookseller.
subfiles.summary: A Maruzen representative visited the Embassy. The reported seller approached engineering students in Kyoto and Osaka; Embassy checks found no such books in specialist Tokyo bookstores.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill on English publication and Maruzen
subfiles.about: Responds to McClure’s questions about English publication and Maruzen’s cooperation.
subfiles.summary: McGraw says new books generally reached England within two or three weeks of United States publication. He will ask Maruzen about confidentiality, the printing location, and contact with the Embassy.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill forwards Maruzen’s reply
subfiles.about: Forwards Maruzen’s report of contact with the Embassy and asks for developments.
subfiles.summary: McGraw asks what the Embassy has learned and whether further action is warranted.

subfiles.title: Maruzen explains its request for confidentiality
subfiles.about: Confirms its Embassy contact and explains why it wishes to remain confidential.
subfiles.summary: Maruzen supplied the Embassy with a bookseller’s circular but fears trade disputes if identified as the informant.

subfiles.title: McClure reports Embassy findings to McGraw-Hill
subfiles.about: Relays the Embassy’s findings about sales of suspected reprints.
subfiles.summary: The reported sales were limited to one Osaka bookseller targeting engineering students. McClure says the Department is seeking an update from the Embassy.

subfiles.title: Exchanges with Japan
subfiles.about: Discusses an unauthorized Japanese edition of Dale Carnegie’s book and book trade relations.
subfiles.summary: The article reports that a Japanese publisher issued a condensed translation without prior permission.

subfiles.title: Department follow-up on McGraw-Hill and other piracy cases
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests further Embassy information on McGraw-Hill piracy and other American copyright cases.
subfiles.summary: The Department encloses Maruzen’s letter and a Publishers’ Weekly excerpt. It says evidence of continued piracy would inform consideration of United States adherence to the international copyright convention.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill asks about action against bookseller
subfiles.about: Asks whether Maruzen could act against the Osaka bookseller.
subfiles.summary: McGraw hopes piracy remains limited and seeks further Embassy information.

subfiles.title: McGraw-Hill follow-up inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests any new information on book piracy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: McGraw asks whether the Department has further developments to share.

subfiles.title: McClure reports no new Embassy information
subfiles.about: Answers McGraw’s follow-up inquiry.
subfiles.summary: No Embassy reply has arrived; the Department is sending a reminder.

subfiles.title: Department reminder on McGraw-Hill copyright infringement
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reminds the Embassy of continuing interest in McGraw-Hill piracy and wider copyright issues.
subfiles.summary: The Department notes McGraw-Hill’s further inquiry and possible renewed congressional and Senate attention to copyright protection.
